why it will never work: this program uses a smart-card reader or a certificate token (A3)
column4: Wine hands the reader over to Linux, so the first step is for Linux to see the token: install pcscd, pcsc-tools and libccid, and run pcsc-scan to see whether it turns up. An honest warning: the reader appearing does not mean the certificate will sign - Brazilian programs tend to ask for the certificate through a Windows path that Linux does not have, and then only the program's supplier can sort it out.

why it will never work: this program uses the CliSiTef card-payment library
column4: The company that makes CliSiTef (Software Express) already publishes a Linux version of it. It is not you who installs it: it is the supplier of your sales system who has to use it. It is worth asking them - on Linux the pinpad usually turns up as /dev/ttyACM0.

why it will never work: this program uses the PayGo card-payment library
column4: PayGo already publishes its library for Linux. It is not you who installs it: it is the supplier of your sales system who has to use it. It is worth asking them.

why it will never work: this program uses ACBrLib for fiscal documents or card payments
column4: ACBrLib is compiled for Linux too, in both 32 and 64 bit. It is not you who installs it: it is your system's supplier who has to use it. It is worth asking them.

why it will never work: this file is a driver installer. Wine lets it run and copy its files, and it reports success - but the part that actually binds a driver to a device does nothing at all, so nothing changes and there is no error to see
column4: In almost every case the device does not need it: Linux already drives the serial and USB bridge chips these discs are for, and the device is usually working already. Run "tandem portas" to see the ports and which device is on each one. If it is a printer, Linux prints through CUPS and the Windows driver is not used. Only a real expansion card or an unusual piece of laboratory hardware truly needs the Windows driver, and for that there is no way through.
